correctness.rationale: The final repaired finding preserves all census formulas. At a=1 the opposite shore is uniform after one update and the two surviving bits obey (c,d)→(1−d,c), giving one four-cycle. At a=2 the opposite shore freezes whenever S=1; an initially unanimous first shore instead forces its sign on the opposite shore at step one. Splitting the fixed points by strict nonunanimous, unanimous, and tied opposite-shore patterns gives the three basin sizes; the step-two count is twice (2^b+H_b)/2. At a≥3, the two canonical first-shore patterns have strict signs, so two strict signs swap and two tied shores are fixed. The frozen proof reversed which pattern updates in the exactly-one-tie case: the tied shore becomes canonical and the strict shore holds. The repair makes this explicit; it implies the strict shore needs a second step exactly when noncanonical, producing the stated N2. No ties can return once lost, so doubly tied states have no distinct predecessors. Complementation gives the polar basin counts. The ordinary rule has the same strict-sign swap and single-tie resolution, giving configuration-wise invariance.
